entries.test: Public measurements of misinformation on Twitter in the months following November 2022 would show whether it increased substantially as cheap AI-generated misinformation spread.
entries.note: The causal context comes from the immediately following sentence. The near-term horizon has passed.

entries.test: Historical pricing and operating-cost data for GPT-3 alternatives would show whether their costs were falling around November 2022.
entries.note: This extracts the sentence's present-tense cost claim faithfully.

entries.test: Public model pricing and reproducible misinformation-generation cost studies would show whether cheaper GPT-3 alternatives drive generation costs toward negligible levels.
entries.note: “Going to zero” has a plain reading as approaching negligible cost. No deadline is stated.
The increase is asserted firmly, but the extracted proposition also includes the explicitly probabilistic exponential-growth claim.

entries.test: Public measurements of machine-generated misinformation and Community Notes coverage and response times would show whether the system falls substantially behind as that misinformation accelerates.
entries.note: “Left in the dust” plainly predicts an inability to keep pace. No deadline is given.
In this advice to Musk, the statement recommends using AI beyond the popular approaches.
“Don’t count on” is an explicit recommendation.

entries.test: Comparative evaluations of misinformation generation and detection using models available in November 2022 would show whether LLMs were unmatched at generation and poor at detection.
entries.note: The emphatic wording still makes substantive comparative capability claims.

entries.test: Reproducible evaluations of contemporaneous LLMs on reasoning about independently verifiable true and false statements would test the asserted absence of that capability.
entries.note: The source says accuracy requires a reference standard of truth; the normalization changes that requirement to reasoning about truth.

entries.test: Public evaluations of LLM scaling would show whether increasing model scale alone produces reliable truth reasoning and misinformation detection.
entries.note: The preceding sentences supply the referent of “this.” A decisive scaling result could refute the undated forecast.
This concludes his recommendation to pursue a different AI approach; it does not exclude retaining LLMs as a component.
